title: Area of a Rectangle Inscribed in an Isosceles Right Triangle
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: A rectangle is inscribed in an isosceles right triangle whose hypotenuse of length 2 lies along the x-axis from (-1, 0) to A(1, 0) and whose right-angled apex is at B(0, 1) on the y-axis. The upper-right vertex of the rectangle is P(x, y) on the segment AB. (a) Express the y-coordinate of P in terms of x. (b) Express the area A of the rectangle in terms of x.

steps.title: Find the Equation of Line Segment AB for Part (a)
steps.explanation: The vertices of the right side of the triangle are B(0, 1) and A(1, 0). The line passing through B(0, 1) and A(1, 0) has slope -1 and y-intercept 1, so its equation is y = 1 - x. Since P(x, y) lies on AB, its y-coordinate is y = 1 - x.
steps.why: In an isosceles right triangle with hypotenuse on [-1, 1], the apex on the positive y-axis has height 1.

steps.title: Determine the Base Width and Height of the Inscribed Rectangle
steps.explanation: By symmetry across the y-axis, the rectangle's base extends from -x to x along the x-axis, giving a width of 2x, while its height is the y-coordinate of P, 1 - x.
steps.why: Inscribing the rectangle symmetrically in the triangle places its left and right vertical sides at -x and x.

steps.title: Write the Area Function A(x) for Part (b)
steps.explanation: Multiply the width 2x by the height 1 - x to obtain the area function A(x) = 2x(1 - x) = 2x - 2x^2 for 0 < x < 1.
steps.why: The area of a rectangle equals the product of its base width and altitude.
